subject: pathology
title: Pseudomembranous Colitis, Ischaemic Colitis, Appendicitis, and Intestinal Carcinoid

steps.tx: Pseudomembranous colitis erupts when Clostridioides difficile toxins A and B, unleashed after antibiotics clear competing flora, volcano fibrin and neutrophil plaques across colonic mucosa with profuse diarrhoea. The toxin colitis is **Clostridioides difficile pseudomembranous colitis**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Antibiotics then watery diarrhoea plus pseudomembranes means C difficile toxins until stool testing clears it.

vis.caption: Clostridioides difficile colitis pathogenesis from dysbiosis to pseudomembrane.

steps.tx: Testing strategy pairs toxin detection with organism evidence because colonisation without toxin production mimics disease in carriers, especially infants, while ileus may silence diarrhoea in fulminant cases. That two step logic is **C difficile toxin based diagnosis**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Toxin, not mere organism presence, makes C difficile disease; fulminant ileus may hide its diarrhoea.

left.title: Colonisation
points: Organism or gene positive, toxin negative

steps.tx: Fulminant disease with ileus, megacolon, perforation risk, and shock needs oral plus rectal vancomycin strategies, surgical consultation early, and faecal microbiota transplantation for recurrences. Escalation defines **fulminant and recurrent C difficile management**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Megacolon and ileus in C difficile disease bring surgeons early; recurrence earns microbiota transplantation discussion.

steps.tx: Ischaemic colitis starves watershed splenic flexure and rectosigmoid mucosa after hypotension, emboli, or vasculitis, bloody diarrhoea and pain in older vascular patients, thumbprinting oedema on imaging. The watershed injury is **ischaemic colitis of watershed colon**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Bloody diarrhoea after hypotension in an older patient at the splenic flexure watershed is ischaemic colitis.

vis.caption: Intestinal patterns across inflammatory, malabsorptive, and structural disease.

steps.tx: Appendicitis obstructs its lumen by lymphoid hyperplasia or faecolith, distending, ischaemia, bacterial invasion, and gangrene toward perforation, pain migrating periumbilical to right iliac fossa. That migration is **acute appendicitis pathophysiology**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Periumbilical pain settling right iliac fossa with anorexia is appendicitis performing its classic migration.

steps.tx: Appendiceal carcinoid, now neuroendocrine tumour, hides in many appendicectomy specimens at the tip, small ones cured by appendicectomy, larger or mesoappendiceal invasive ones earning right hemicolectomy discussion. Size decides: **appendiceal neuroendocrine tumour management by size**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: An incidental two centimetre appendiceal carcinoid earns hemicolectomy talk; a tiny tip lesion is already cured.

steps.tx: Intestinal carcinoid of midgut secretes serotonin and tachykinins, desmoplastically kinking bowel and mesentery, syndrome appearing when liver metastases bypass first pass inactivation. That fibrosis is **midgut neuroendocrine tumour desmoplasia**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Midgut carcinoids kink bowel with fibrosis years before flushing announces their liver metastases.

steps.tx: Colonic ischaemia usually heals conservatively because collateral flow rescues mucosa, while gangrene, perforation, or persistent sepsis converts management surgical, separating transient from transmural disease. That fork is **transient versus gangrenous ischaemic colitis**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Most ischaemic colitis heals with support; peritonism or sepsis means gangrene and a surgeon.
